item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1vmga_ and d1y6xa1 are in the same all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily, a.204.1 (SUNID 101386), supporting probable remote common ancestry. They are not in the same family: d1vmga_ is MazG-like, a.204.1.2 (SUNID 116993), whereas d1y6xa1 is HisE-like (PRA-PH), a.204.1.4 (SUNID 140797). Thus they also share fold a.204 and class a, but the meaningful homology claim is at superfamily—not family—level. This classification does not justify transferring HisE’s phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase activity, histidine-biosynthesis role, substrate specificity, catalytic residues, or kinetics to d1vmga_; nor does it justify assigning MazG-specific activity to d1y6xa1. In particular, SCOPe labels d1vmga_ as a structural-genomics target whose protein node is hypothetical, so “MazG-like” is not an experimental functional determination. Exact function would require independent evidence such as biochemical assays, conserved active-site and sequence analysis, ligand-bound structural evidence, or corroborating genomic context. Either structure may be a remote structural template for the shared core, but family-specific loops, active sites, and functional annotations should not be transferred without that evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__compare_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/homology"]}]}
